title: Lawrence the deacon (258)
hookLine: ordered to hand over the Church's treasures, he brings the poor

cards: Bring me the treasures of the Church. That's the demand put to a deacon in Rome named Lawrence. Tradition says the officials expected gold and silver.
Lawrence doesn't argue, and he doesn't run. He promises to show them. The next day he arrives with a crowd behind him: the poor of the church, the people it fed and looked after.
He points at them. These, he says, are the treasures of the Church.

teach.b: The story is told by Ambrose, a bishop writing in a later generation. First, what a deacon was for.
In the Acts of the Apostles, the Christians in Jerusalem complain that their widows are being overlooked in the daily care.
The apostles don't want to leave preaching to serve tables, so seven men are chosen to look after it. The church came to call that ministry the deacon's.
In Justin's Sunday, the deacons carry the bread to those who are absent, and the collection goes to orphans, widows and strangers. Lawrence served in that line, in Rome. Second, his bishop.
Ambrose says Lawrence watched his bishop, Sixtus, being led away to die, and cried out: where are you going, father, without your son? Sixtus told him he would follow soon. Third, the treasures.
When the order comes to hand over the Church's wealth, Lawrence shows them the people.
In the same book, Ambrose argues that the Church has gold to spend on those in need, not to store up, and adds that the poor truly were treasures, because Christ lives in them.

Tradition, which Ambrose repeats, says Lawrence was put to death by being roasted, and that he joked even then: this side's done, turn me over. Whatever the details, his name is still read in the Roman Canon at Mass.
And the story keeps asking every parish the same question: when someone asks to see your treasure, who do you point at?

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Lawrence in the Church's calendar, and deacons today still proclaim the Gospel at Mass and are charged with service, especially to the poor.

games.q: you're Lawrence. a Roman official orders you to bring the treasures of the Church. what do you bring?
games.why: Ambrose says Lawrence gathered the poor and said: these are the treasures of the Church. Christ lives in them.

practice: Let one person come to mind who is poor, in money or in some other way: a man on the same corner, a family your parish helps, a lonely neighbor; use a name if you know one.
Look at them the way Lawrence did, as what the Church would point at if someone asked to see its wealth, and notice what changes in you. If you pray, say their name to God.

wordCard.voice: Lawrence the deacon. The Roman deacon who, ordered to hand over the Church's treasures, brought the poor. Today's word.
